chapter: Luck, tricks and the Bourbon Street job
title: Emptying a Bourbon Street club, then filling it with a powder trick
summary: Playing at a Bourbon Street club near the Haymarket with no customers, he sent John Smith for powder and the place packed that night. The band got paid nightly and left before Christmas.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: He was playing right on Bourbon Street at the old Haymarket. Right there, I'm going to tell you where that was Mr. Bill, and right there going, a couple blocks going toward Conair Street. Yeah. On the corner there. Right on the corner. You know right on the corner there, you see right on the corner they got a place there where they don't show nothing but, but have shows there I believe. Yeah. On this side the bank it.
Yeah, maybe it's El Morocco or something. Yeah, round in there.

Round Long in there, but it's about a couple blocks from Conair Street. Yeah. You know. So the Haymarket was up in there somewhere, up in there, in that block there, you know. So this old man, you know, he had a nightclub and he couldn't get nobody in that club. Nobody wouldn't come there. And with Chico was playing, he had a nightclub across the street.
Yeah.
What's this guy name in his wife's house? Got this man in here now.
Sid DeVilla for a while had one there.
Oh, no. Prima.
Yeah. Leon Prima.
Yeah, he crossed the street here. Yeah. You see? All right. So we was playing there, you know.
So couldn't get nobody in that play.

So we was talking, me and John, you know. I said, John, we going to get somebody in this place here tonight. So I said, man you go, I said go to the drugs, so he went on Conair and Rapporty. He went and got some, I told him to get the whole grain, you know. He went and got the powder. And man, when he came back he had powder all over his clothes, all over his face.
I asked him, I said, what are you care for man?
I said, look at you being a flower bear, you know. So he had it all over his clothes. I said, oh, I said, that was you done wrong. Because good clothes. All on his clothes that way.
But he said, I'll spray.

And you know what I'm saying Mr. Bill? I wouldn't tell you what, you know we had some people in that place. But they did pack it, huh? Yeah, well it's funny how that'll work sometimes. And look, and from that day we never told that man how that people come to the company. And well all right, that very night we did that, and that very night we left. See we left, it was going to be on the Christmas, you see. They was going to play somewhere else, going somewhere else and play, you see. And the boy that got tied playing. We played a long time on Bourbon Street there. So, and from that time we never told the old man nothing. You know what I mean? So this old man, you know, since he couldn't get nobody in his club, he used to have a fellow used to come there. Every night that fellow would come, musical tax, you know. He used to come collect. Well the old man, the old man owed about $500 musical tax. But every time he come, he never gets to catch the old man. The old man duck him, you know. So, so that's the only time that old man made money that night. That one, that one special night. But all them other nights we played there, couldn't get nobody up in that place. Everybody passing, you know what I mean? They going, you know, live for me, cross the street. All them days there, plenty, you know what I mean? There's a lot of bands on Bourbon Street. More than they got there now. They ain't got no band there now, you see. So, couldn't get nobody in that place.
Yeah, it was a nice place, you know what I mean?

And all and things, but the question, but I don't know. And look, he used to have nice flow shows and all, you know what I mean? Yeah, he used to have flow show, different time of the night, you know what I mean? Certain time, you know, show come in, you know what I mean? Late show, first show and all that kind of stuff like that, you know what I mean?
And he's pretty fair old man, so, but just see, some kind of way, I don't know.
He just couldn't get nobody in there, till we got him in that night.
Yeah, sometimes bad luck, they just happen to know about the place.
Yeah, that's right, yeah, that's right. So, man, so we would tell, we never told old man that. Never did tell him.
No, no, we never told.
And you see how we used to do? You see, we supposed to get paid about a week, you see. But we, them boys didn't want the money like that. We'd get our money every night.
Every night, yeah, well it's easier than we had something to spend with it. Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah.
We'd get it, yeah, we'd get it every night. So, alright. So, when we left from there, that was all. Yeah. And next day, I'll be there, well, that next day was going to be Christmas.
That's right.
And we'd going, in the country, going somewhere to play, now we left. And we never just went back no more there. You know what I mean? Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
